_help.about: [The sacred fig wired (Uniques; design §CL) — its faint path in from a road, roots on old stone, the leaves' own flutter and the hood down NOT WIRED YET] One-of-a-kind places: each appears exactly once in a world. The sites pass (§CK) places it where its `where` holds, off a road like the §BC landmarks (40-120 m from the trail and out of sight of it, with a faint path in), built to the composition rules (LOOK_REFERENCE: a straight last approach, walls either side, an apron in front). It is never a camp and never a ruin. Restart after editing.
_help.fields: name · count_per_world (always 1) · where (biomes in order of preference; the first the world has wins; other: plain words) · tree (the species and how this one specimen differs from the wild ones) · figure (who is there: the shared cloaked rig, pose, colours, behaviour) · ground (the clearing) · sound · log (the line written the first time you come within reach) · open (calls still with the designer).
_help.rig: Every figure uses the player's cloaked rig (one rig, §0); a figure here is a pose and a palette, never a new body. The player's indigo-and-rust is reserved for the player.

sacred_fig.name: The sacred fig

where.other: A level clearing on a low rise in tropical dry forest (else monsoon jungle, else savanna woodland), off a road, not in a wetland or on a slope; the oldest tree for kilometres. If old stone is near (a ruin wall, a boulder), the tree grows out of it.

tree.size: Past the top of the species' band: about 30 m tall, the crown 35-45 m across, the trunk a fused mass of old grey stems several metres round.
tree.notes: Heart-shaped leaves with a long drip-tip tail on long, slender stalks, so they tremble in still air (the wind shader has no per-species flutter yet: §CL asks for one here). Smooth pale grey bark. Roots gripping stone where it started on a wall. Purple-black figs in pairs in the leaf axils in season; birds and bats in the crown.

figure.rig: the cloaked figure, folk scale (~1.7 m standing)
figure.pose: seated in meditation under the crown on the east side of the trunk, facing east: legs crossed, hands resting together in the lap, back straight, eyes closed, hood down

robe.notes: an ochre robe; one shade throughout, no pattern

figure.moves: never, but to breathe; nothing the player does changes that

sacred_fig.ground: Bare swept earth in a ring under the crown, fallen leaves at its edge; a few flat stones; no fire, no tools, no store.
sacred_fig.sound: The leaves' dry rustle over everything; birds in the crown by day.
sacred_fig.log: Someone sits beneath the old fig, very still.
open: Naming (Mike): Mike asked for the Buddha meditating beneath it. Play names nobody (§BO keeps real names out of play), so the default is no name and the image speaks for itself; say if the log or a label should name him.
Night (Mike): does the dark keep away from this place, a still circle with no fire? Default: no special rule until Mike decides.

wandering_fire.name: The wandering fire

where.other: The hot desert and its edges; they walk on and off the roads, a few kilometres a day, and never settle.

figures.rig: the cloaked figure, folk scale; one set apart by his robe, the twelve in the desert folk's palette (cloaks.json)

robe.notes: undyed pale wool, hood down; first guess

wandering_fire.day: They walk (§BF's pace, on and off the road), carrying their flame as a coal in an ember carrier (§BP: fire is never made).
wandering_fire.dusk: They lay a fire where they are from what the desert gives (fuel.json: scrub, dung), and sit round it: §CY.2's circle loops (watch the fire, warm hands, eat, doze), no pipe.
wandering_fire.dawn: They walk on and leave the ring: a line of cold fire rings a day's walk apart is their trail.

fire.note: a safe circle like any fire (§BA); its glow is how you find them at night (§CV)

wandering_fire.log: Thirteen sit round a fire in the sand.
open: Naming (Mike): default as the fig, play names nobody.
Night (Mike): does the dark keep off their circle when the fire burns low? Default: no special rule.
Giving (Mike): anything beyond a coal? Default: nothing.
wandering_fire._help: The second one-of-a-kind and the first that moves (WanderingFire; design §DP): thirteen in the desert who walk by day and sit by a carried fire at night, leaving a trail of cold rings. Built: each night's place is a pure function of the world's seed and the clock (2.5-5 km a day, hot desert or thorn scrub, never standing water); they walk 06:30-17:30, lay and light the fire at 18:00 (a FireStore like any, a safe circle, a coal free to take), sit round it till dawn; the last nights' rings lie cold. Not built: §CY.2's circle loops (they sit still), the hood down (the rig has no bare head). Restart after editing.

road_regulars._help: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DM.7, §DQ] The road regulars: a cast of named one-of-a-kind figures on the shared rig, each with ONE habit tied to the real clock, one stretch and one hour (§DM.7, cast open). Mute (§BF) except as §DJ allows; the habit is the personality. The first entry is §DQ's rider; §DM.7's three starters (the pilgrim at dawn, the old one on the milestone, the dog) are not written until Mike and Claude build the cast.

ox_rider.name: The old man on his ox
ox_rider.rules: a §BF traveller (mute, never stops for you, the hood turns and holds a beat, the dark ignores him) who rides
ox_rider.stretch: the high roads of one great range (§CR.4), toward its highest pass, westward
ox_rider.hours: rides by day at the ox's pace (under the walk); at dusk stops where he is, the ox grazes, no fire; at dawn rides on

mount.notes: a domestic ox, not a buffalo (Mike): heavy, slow, horns curving forward and out, a dull black-brown coat (#2A2220), no load and no plough; a creature body (§0), new; the rider is the shared rig seated on it, hood up, a plain dark robe (first guess)

ox_rider.log: An old man rides an ox up the pass road, slowly.

gate.what: a gatehouse at the highest pass of his range: a small camp with its keeper (§BL, one or two folk), and the book he left lying there
gate.open: Mike: in or out (one line to strike)

open: Naming (Mike): default as the fig, play names nobody.
The gate, its keeper and the book: written in as a first guess.
